F1: The timeout context inherits request cancellation, so the asynchronous legacy write can be canceled after the primary write succeeds.
F2: Legacy Update reapplies the original update transformation to its own potentially stale object instead of using the primary storage result.
F3: Independent goroutines can apply same-resource writes out of order and leave legacy storage inconsistent with primary storage.
F4: The changed metric calls misattribute backend failures and use the object name as a kind label, making observations inaccurate and high-cardinality.
F5: The shared mocks weaken test coverage, but this is a test-quality gap rather than a defect in changed production behavior.
